odd_even.verdict_text: The two dips are different sizes — odd transits dip 0.399% but even transits dip 0.274% (31% apart). That is the classic sign of an eclipsing binary whose real period is twice the candidate period.

kill_reason: odd/even alternating eclipse depths at 2P (odd 0.399% vs even 0.274%, 31% apart); double-period CONFIRMS with deep unequal eclipses (2.155% / 1.363%) at refined 25.9413 d plus an ellipsoidal wave +0.592% @ 12.5 sigma. On-target twin-star eclipsing binary; true period ~25.94 d, the sweep's 13.1433 d is the half-period alias.

double_period.verdict_text: The light between the eclipses is not flat — at the quarter-orbit points the system brightens to 1.0080 while the shoulders beside the eclipses sit at 1.0020: a 0.59% wave at 12σ. That brightening is two stars squeezed out of round by each other's gravity, showing us their wider sides twice per orbit — a planet is far too light to bend its star like this. These are twin stars orbiting every 25.94 days, not a planet.
double_period.note: Post-gate diagnostic (driver gated at stage b); run to complete the brief's (a)-(c) fold set.

reclassification_note: Fold completion AGREES with the stamp's suspicion and IDENTIFIES the object. The in-sweep 'fails persistence - blend-suspect' is the persistence module's generic label for a non-constant-depth alias signal; it is refined here, not overturned in substance: the signal is not a planet train. The blend reading specifically is excluded - contratio 0.026 (clean aperture) and an on-target ellipsoidal wave - this binary is the target star itself.
